# Shapiro-Wilk Normality Test
Test using Shapiro-Wilk normality test the Ethereum returns for trading data every five minutes, from August 7, 2015 to September 15, 2026.

## Calibrating the Dataset
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(readr)
eth_raw <- read_csv("C:/Users/Angelo/Downloads/ETHUSDT-5m-1483228800000-1788825599999-selected-columns.csv")
View(eth_raw)
Eth_Close <- eth_raw$Close
Close_Time <- eth_raw$`Close time`
```
```{r}
eth_clean <- eth_raw %>%
  mutate(datetime = as_datetime(eth_raw$`Close time`)) %>%
  arrange(datetime) %>%
  filter(datetime >= ymd_hms("2026-09-15 23:59:59"))
```

## We get the Ethereum returns
```{r}
eth_returns <- eth_clean %>%
  mutate(E_Returns = log(Close / lag(Close))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(E_Returns) & is.finite(E_Returns))
```

## Shapiro-Wilk Test
Since the Shapiro-Wilk test is limited to 5000 samples in R, we select 5000 random samples from the dataset.
```{r}
eth_sample <- eth_returns %>% slice_sample(n = 5000)

shapiro_result <- shapiro.test(eth_sample$E_Returns)
shapiro_result
```
